meta.title: Implementation plan: work packages
meta.status: Active implementation; evidence and remaining gates tracked per work package

phases.name: Foundations and spikes
phases.goal: Fix the repository structure and test harness, and answer the open technical questions before building on them.
exit: Multi-module build with enforced runtime/control boundary is green in CI
Acceptance-test harness marks test status automatically
Spikes A to E are closed with an ADR each; remaining unknowns have an owner and a validation point
Acceptance status reporting includes Maven Failsafe reports for process-level integration tests
Standalone spike tests have reproducible commands and an explicit CI or manual verification policy

phases.name: Secure governed execution core
phases.goal: A process that runs durably, authenticates people and agents, enforces policy outside the agent, involves humans, and survives failure with explicit idempotency and recovery semantics for business effects.
exit: One end-to-end governed case runs, survives kill -9 and completes once
Traces show workflow, agent, tool and model spans under one correlation id

phases.name: Agent capability
phases.goal: Agents plan and re-plan, use tools and knowledge, remember within scope, collaborate with other agents and with people, all inside the bounds from phase 1.
exit: An unstructured request is resolved by a supervisor agent with two specialists, one over A2A
Limits stop a runaway agent; injected attacks are rejected

phases.name: Governed lifecycle and authority
phases.goal: Everything that changes agent behavior is inventoried, versioned, approved and reversible; in-flight work is pinned; emergency control works without the admin service.
exit: Runtime keeps working with the control application stopped
Revoking a tool or model stops active and waiting tasks within the agreed bound

phases.name: Operations and deployment
phases.goal: The platform can be backed up, upgraded, deployed on several environments, isolated per tenant and scaled with evidence.
exit: T18, T20, T21, T24 pass
Restore and rolling-upgrade drills are automated in CI or a scheduled job
Published RTO and RPO measured, not assumed

phases.name: Quality and model governance
phases.goal: Quality is measured before release and in production; models are chosen by configuration and evaluated consistently.
exit: T10, T31, T38, T39 pass
A quality drop raises an alert and opens a gate review
The same task runs on two providers and a self-hosted model

phases.name: Lifecycle tooling, coexistence and console
phases.goal: Authors, operators and approvers get tooling; legacy coexistence and the governance assistant are delivered.
exit: T27, T29, T33 pass
Operators use the console for all routine tasks; every action is API-backed and audited
All 39 acceptance tests are automated

rules: Each unfinished work package has exactly one implementation owner and the other agent as reviewer. Completed packages are historical evidence, outside both backlogs; regression fixes go through their path owner.

The numbered rows are priority queues, not a promise of equal effort or simultaneous delivery. Each agent works on one implementation PR at a time and picks the first unblocked row; review the other agent promptly before starting another PR.

An After gate means the needed API, implementation and failure tests have merged and been reviewed, not merely proposed. Original start dependencies remain visible in the detailed checklist. WP-105 is the only explicitly accepted partial baseline for starting dependent work; its remaining recovery gate closes after WP-108/WP-107/WP-109. WP-102 gates are interface-specific, not whole-package closure: WP-103/WP-106/WP-404 need merged verified-caller and tenant/authority mapping with denial tests; WP-205/WP-206 need merged scoped caller and delegation-grant verification; WP-207 needs the merged exchanged-credential/target/TTL/replay contract and interoperability evidence for its selected provider; WP-604 needs merged verified user-delegation and caller guards. Real-Keycloak evidence is a separate WP-102 closure gate and does not block consumers of already evidenced interfaces. If Keycloak rejects actor_token/act semantics, Claude requests a GPT-owned ADR/contract handoff before any affected provider-dependent consumer proceeds.

WP-103 and WP-303 may merge useful increments while their consumer/freshness/evaluation closure gates remain partial. A merged prerequisite is usable only for its evidenced interface; no package becomes completed until every existing deliverable and acceptance gate passes.

Use separate branches from current main: gpt/<WP-id>-<scope> and claude/<WP-id>-<scope>. Do not edit the other agent branch, shared checkout, or write areas. Rebase after every prerequisite merge and rerun affected checks.

For a cross-area change, write docs/handoffs/<agent>/<WP-id>.md with producer/consumer, exact affected paths, port/schema/config proposal, acceptance/failure cases and evidence. The registered writer implements and merges that small handoff before the consumer depends on it. It is a subtask of the requesting package, never a second owner of the same work package.

Shared-file writes are serialized by GPT integration ownership. Claude must request contract, migration, build, configuration, lifecycle, acceptance-status and tracking changes; GPT requests Claude-owned policy/caller/audit/agent edits the same way. No simultaneous edits to a shared file, including generated documents.

Before each implementation PR merges, the other agent reviews the exact current head SHA for behavior, boundary bypasses and failure/recovery cases, verifies relevant tests independently, and records findings plus a pass/request-changes verdict. Any later code change requires another review of the new head; unresolved material findings block merge.

If both agents use the same GitHub identity, record reviewer=GPT or reviewer=Claude, head SHA, commands/results and verdict explicitly in the PR review/comment; do not claim a distinct GitHub approval or self-review. GPT updates execution status after each review, implementation start and merge; record outstanding findings and the reviewed SHA without claiming a later head was approved.

GPT collects Claude evidence and updates plan/status JSON, CHANGELOG and generated TODO in a serialized integration commit on main or the current integration PR. A package is not closed before that update, reciprocal review and green CI. Planning this work does not change current implementation or acceptance status.

Claude reviews this ownership/dependency plan and GPT addresses recorded findings. WP-108 starts on the merged WP-105 core independently of WP-102 design/real-IdP evidence; GPT and Claude may implement their owned first packages concurrently. Cross-area consumers still wait for their required merged interface handoffs. Claude review of the exact implementation head, no unresolved material findings, and passing CI remain mandatory before GPT merges. Preserve outcome-only research documentation and do not restore spike implementations.
